title: Impinj M730 UHF Inlay — Cost-Optimized RAIN RFID for Retail Source Tagging
summary: The Impinj M730 (Monza R6 silicon class) is the volume retail workhorse of the M700 family — 96-bit EPC, ISO/IEC 18000-63 / EPC Gen2 v2 compliant, and engineered for the lowest practical silicon ASP at billion-tag scale. Proud Tek supplies M730 inlays in dry-inlay, wet-inlay and finished-label converted form for global retail apparel source tagging, footwear, accessories and high-volume FMCG serialization programs that require SGTIN-96 EPC encoding without the additional cost of User memory or chip-level cryptographic features.
heroPoints: Cost-optimized for billion-tag scale — sub-cent silicon ASP at multi-million-piece annual volumes makes the M730 the standard choice for global retail source-tagging programs encoding 10-50 billion items per year.

96-bit EPC + 96-bit serialized TID — sufficient for full SGTIN-96 (GS1 Tag Data Standard 2.0) encoding, with a globally unique factory-programmed TID (Impinj E280-1160 prefix) for inventory deduplication and anti-cloning audit trails.

Autotune impedance matching — Impinj's on-chip auto-tune circuit re-matches the antenna at every power-up, recovering performance lost to mixed-substrate retail environments (cardboard, polybag, hangtag, on-glass).

sections.title: Why the M730 dominates retail source tagging
bullets: Silicon ASP — Impinj sells M730 wafer at the most competitive UHF chip pricing in the global market because the chip's feature set is intentionally minimal: 96-bit EPC, factory-serialized TID, and no User memory. There is nothing on the silicon that does not directly serve high-volume retail SGTIN-96 encoding.

Encoder throughput — the M730 supports the standard EPC Gen2 v2 BlockWrite command and tolerates the high-temperature, high-RF-density environment of a retail printer-applicator (e.g. Printronix T8000, Zebra ZT411) running at 1,000+ tags per minute.

Inlay ecosystem — every major converter (Avery Dennison/Smartrac, Arizon, HID, Beontag, SML, Trace ID) maintains M730 reference inlays in catalog antenna designs (AD-227, AD-237, AD-661 and equivalents). New SKU rollouts are typically 2-4 weeks ex-stock.

Reader compatibility — the M730 is fully ISO/IEC 18000-63 + EPC Gen2 v2 compliant. Every fixed reader (Impinj R700, Zebra FX9600), every handheld (Zebra MC3300xR, Impinj IPJ-R0510), and every printer-encoder reads and writes the M730 with no firmware change.

sections.title: What the M730 is NOT the right fit for
bullets: Brand protection or anti-counterfeiting — the M730 does not implement EPC Gen2 v2 Authenticate or Untraceable. For cryptographic chip-authenticity programs choose the Impinj M750 (Monza R6-P) or NXP UCODE 9 instead.

Pharmaceutical serialization with on-tag User data — the M730 has 0 bits of User memory. DSCSA / EU FMD encoded data must live in a backend database keyed by EPC. If you need on-tag data (batch, expiration, encrypted serial), choose the M750 (32-bit User), Higgs-9 (128-bit User) or UCODE 9 (32-224-bit configurable).

EU Digital Product Passport (DPP) UHF tier — DPP requirements typically include User memory for the DPP URL pointer plus chip-level Authenticate. M730 is insufficient on both counts; use UCODE 9 or M750.
Sensor or specialty applications — no sensor variant exists in the M730 line. Cold-chain moisture sensing requires UCODE 9xe; tamper detection at UHF requires a different specialty silicon.

sections.title: Standard antenna configurations Proud Tek supplies
bullets: Far-field general-purpose (~70 × 14 mm) — the standard retail and supply-chain reference inlay for hangtags, pallet labels, carton labels.
Compact retail (~44 × 14 mm) — for jewelry, eyewear, accessories and small-item apparel where the inlay must fit inside a 50 × 25 mm hangtag.
On-metal (with foam spacer or specialty antenna) — read range 1.5-2.5 m on metal; choose the M750 instead if you need wider on-metal margin via the R6-P's improved sensitivity.
On-liquid (foam-isolated label, optimized for cosmetics and beverage) — read range 1.0-2.0 m; the M730 is the cost-optimized choice for high-volume FMCG.
Custom antenna designs — Proud Tek + partner antenna engineers turn around custom M730 antenna designs in 6-10 weeks from spec to first samples; production tooling adds 2-4 weeks.

faq.question: What is the difference between the Impinj M730 and the M750?
faq.answer: The M730 (Monza R6 class) is the cost-optimized variant: 96-bit EPC, no User memory, no EPC Gen2 v2 Authenticate or Untraceable. The M750 (Monza R6-P class) adds 32 bits of User memory plus full Authenticate and Untraceable support, at a ~30% silicon-ASP premium. Choose M730 for pure SGTIN-96 retail volume; choose M750 if you need brand-authentication, retail-privacy at POS, or any User memory.

faq.question: Is the M730 the same chip as the Monza R6?
faq.answer: Yes — Impinj rebranded the Monza R6 silicon as the M730 as part of the M700-series naming refresh. Datasheets, EPC behavior and TID prefix (E280-1160) are unchanged. Existing readers, encoders and inlays branded as Monza R6 are interoperable with M730 inlays.

faq.question: What read range can I expect from a Proud Tek M730 inlay?
faq.answer: In free-air on a paper hangtag with an Impinj R700 reader at +30 dBm EIRP, expect 8-10 m. On apparel hangtags 6-8 m. On metal with a foam-spaced specialty antenna 1.5-2.5 m. On liquid (cosmetics/beverage) with a foam-isolated label 1.0-2.0 m. Pallet portal read rates are 98-99% on dense loads. Real numbers depend on antenna design, reader power and the specific deployment substrate.

faq.question: Can the M730 be used with my existing Impinj R700 / Zebra FX9600 reader fleet?
faq.answer: Yes. The M730 is fully ISO/IEC 18000-63 + EPC Gen2 v2 compliant; every standards-compliant fixed reader, handheld and printer-encoder reads/writes it with no firmware change. The advanced EPC Gen2 v2 commands (Untraceable, Authenticate, Hide-EPC) that Impinj M750 / NXP UCODE 9 implement are not available on the M730 — but the basic inventory and read/write commands work identically.

faq.question: What MOQ does Proud Tek offer for M730 inlays?
faq.answer: 10,000 pieces for stock antenna designs (general-purpose far-field, compact retail, on-metal, on-liquid, windshield). For custom antenna designs MOQ is typically 50,000-100,000 pieces depending on tooling depth. Sample sets of 100-500 pieces are available for evaluation.
